root_cause.text: The GCS page protection macros (_PAGE_GCS and _PAGE_GCS_RO) unconditionally set the PTE_SHARED bits (bits 8-9) without considering that under FEAT_LPA2 these bits are repurposed as output address bits 50-51, resulting in corrupted page table entries and a translation fault when creating GCS mappings on systems with LPA2 enabled.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "When FEAT_LPA2 is enabled, bits 8-9 of the PTE replace the shareability attribute with bits 50-51 of the output address. The _PAGE_GCS{,_RO} definitions include the PTE_SHARED bits as 0b11 ... but using this macro directly leads to the following panic." The patch fixes this by introducing a `gcs_page_prot` variable that clears PTE_SHARED when LPA2 is enabled, mirroring the existing handling for `protection_map`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unused PAGE_GCS and PAGE_GCS_RO macro definitions as they are no longer needed; the constants are used directly where required.
intent_record.what: Removed two preprocessor macro definitions: #define PAGE_GCS __pgprot(_PAGE_GCS) and #define PAGE_GCS_RO __pgprot(_PAGE_GCS_RO).
intent_record.how: These macros are no longer available for use in the codebase. The underlying page protection constants _PAGE_GCS and _PAGE_GCS_RO remain defined and are still used directly in the PIE_E0 macro definition. Any code relying on PAGE_GCS or PAGE_GCS_RO will fail to compile until updated.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a read-only after init global constant `gcs_page_prot` initialized with `_PAGE_GCS_RO` to prepare page protection for GCS pages.
intent_record.what: Added a new static variable `gcs_page_prot` of type `ptdesc_t`, marked `__ro_after_init`, initialized to `_PAGE_GCS_RO`, after the `protection_map` array.
intent_record.how: Introduces a constant page protection descriptor for GCS (Guard Control Store) pages with read-only access; can be used later to assign protection attributes to GCS memory regions.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix missing clearing of PTE_SHARED bit from gcs_page_prot when LPA2 is enabled, ensuring consistent shareability attribute handling for GCS pages.
intent_record.what: Added braces around the existing loop under the lpa2_is_enabled() condition and inserted a new line that clears the PTE_SHARED bit from gcs_page_prot.
intent_record.how: When lpa2_is_enabled() is true, the code now also clears the PTE_SHARED bit from gcs_page_prot, in addition to clearing it from all entries in the protection_map array.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix GCS page protection by using the platform-specific gcs_page_prot variable instead of a hardcoded constant.
intent_record.what: In the function vm_get_page_prot, the assignment of 'prot' inside the condition for system_supports_gcs() with VM_SHADOW_STACK has been changed from the constant '_PAGE_GCS_RO' to the variable 'gcs_page_prot'.
intent_record.how: Instead of always using the fixed page protection _PAGE_GCS_RO for GCS shadow stack pages, the code now uses the dynamically determined 'gcs_page_prot' variable, which allows the kernel to apply different protection attributes based on system configuration or runtime conditions.

relevance_review.reason: The group removes the exact macros (_PAGE_GCS and _PAGE_GCS_RO) that are the root cause of the vulnerability. Even though described as removing unused definitions, they are the macros that improperly set PTE_SHARED bits under FEAT_LPA2, causing page table corruption. The removal directly addresses the vulnerability.

The group adds a constant `gcs_page_prot` initialized with `_PAGE_GCS_RO`, which is one of the flawed macros that unconditionally set PTE_SHARED bits without considering FEAT_LPA2. This change does not modify or fix the root cause; it merely uses the existing problematic macro, thus not addressing the vulnerability.

The group directly addresses the root cause by fixing the missing clearing of the PTE_SHARED bit when LPA2 is enabled, preventing corruption of page table entries and translation faults on systems with LPA2.

The group directly addresses the root cause by replacing a hardcoded constant that unconditionally sets the PTE_SHARED bits with a platform-specific variable, which is necessary to avoid corruption under FEAT_LPA2 that repurposes those bits.

candidates.rationale: This macro unconditionally includes _PAGE_DEFAULT which sets PTE_SHARED bits (bits 8-9). Under FEAT_LPA2 these bits are repurposed as output address bits 50-51, leading to corrupted page table entries and translation faults when GCS mappings are created on systems with LPA2 enabled.
Similarly, this macro unconditionally includes _PAGE_DEFAULT with PTE_SHARED, causing the same corruption issue on LPA2 systems for read-only GCS pages.
This wrapper macro inherits the problematic _PAGE_GCS definition and is used in page protection tables, propagating the unconditional PTE_SHARED setting.
This wrapper macro inherits the problematic _PAGE_GCS_RO definition and is used for read-only GCS pages, also unconditionally setting PTE_SHARED.

This statement directly assigns the vulnerable _PAGE_GCS_RO macro to the page protection when creating GCS mappings, introducing the unconditional PTE_SHARED bits that cause corruption on LPA2 systems.
